The Asymptotic Number of Anticodes in Hamming Spaces

1 Introduction

Anticodes are fundamental objects in coding theory and extremal combinatorics. Whereas error-correcting codes are designed to keep codewords sufficiently far apart, anticodes consist of sets of words whose pairwise distances are bounded from above. This simple definition gives rise to a rich class of combinatorial structures whose properties depend on the underlying metric and the imposed diameter constraint.

The study of anticodes has a long history, particularly in connection with classical extremal problems. A central question has been to determine the maximum cardinality of an anticode of prescribed diameter. In Hamming spaces, classical diametric theorems determine the maximum size of such families and describe the geometry of extremal configurations in a wide range of parameter regimes [14, 1, 2].

Beyond their intrinsic combinatorial interest, anticodes play an important role in coding theory. In particular, the code–anticode bound relates the minimum distance of a code to the diameter and cardinality of an anticode, generalizing the sphere-packing bound in suitable metric spaces [3].

Alongside these extremal questions, related enumeration questions have been studied for error-correcting codes in various metrics and algebraic settings (see, e.g., [5, 7, 10, 16] and references therein). Such results illustrate the value of enumeration in understanding large families of combinatorial objects. However, codes and anticodes satisfy fundamentally different distance constraints, so enumeration results for codes do not directly determine the number of anticodes.

While extremal results determine how large an anticode can be, a different question is how many anticodes satisfy a prescribed diameter constraint. In this paper, we study this question asymptotically. Asymptotic enumeration can reveal how the number of anticodes grows with the parameters of the ambient space and thus provide a broader perspective on the structure of these families.

In this work, we count anticodes in the ambient space (where is a prime power), equipped with the Hamming distance, which counts the coordinates in which two vectors differ. For a set , we write for its diameter. A set of points with diameter at most is called a -anticode. Let be the family of all -anticodes. We further distinguish between general anticodes and linear ones, i.e., those that form a subspace of . In particular, linear anticodes form a subclass of general anticodes.

Our initial approach to count the number of maximal anticodes was to combine the hypergraph container method with stability results for extremal anticodes. For , Frankl’s stability theorem [8] makes this approach effective in certain regimes. For , stability is known when the codiameter is fixed, but we are not aware of a stability result that applies uniformly over the range of diameters considered here.

The paper is organized as follows. In Section 2, we collect the extremal, structural, and asymptotic tools used throughout the paper. In Section 3, we count general anticodes by passing to inclusion-maximal anticodes and applying the Helly-type theorem for Hamming balls. In Section 4, we count linear anticodes by first choosing their support and then counting full-support subspaces on that support. We treat fixed, sublinear, and linear diameters and the near-full regime separately, and conclude the section with the probabilistic improvement for . Finally, in Section 5, we place our results in broader context, and discuss extensions to growing field size and to codes with restricted distances.

5 Conclusion, further discussion, and open problems

We conclude this paper by explaining the broader implications of our counts, stating some related results on the number of anticodes, and some ideas for further research.

5.1 Broader implications

Our results reveal an interesting difference between the asymptotic behavior of general and linear anticodes. In the general setting, for , excluding the binary endpoint and , the asymptotic number of anticodes of a prescribed diameter is governed, on the logarithmic scale, by the number of subsets of one maximum anticode. In other words, counting these subsets already gives the correct leading term in the logarithm of the total count. As a consequence, the number of inclusion-maximal anticodes is asymptotically negligible compared with the total number of anticodes.

The situation is different in the linear setting. Counting subspaces of one maximum linear anticode need not give the correct leading term on the logarithmic scale. We organize all linear anticodes according to their support, using the one-to-one correspondence between codes with a prescribed support and full-support codes on those coordinates. This decomposition gives our asymptotic estimates and bounds. These contrasting behaviors demonstrate that imposing linearity fundamentally changes the asymptotic growth of the number of anticodes.
